title: Audit-forwarder: customer-managed S3 proxy + cross-account STS and offline ingest options
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers deploying Redwood Private/VPC or air-gapped on-prem expect the audit event pipeline to land in customer-managed object storage (S3/GCS/Azure) while maintaining audit integrity, end-to-end encryption controls (CMEK), and operational observability. Current forwarding options either require direct signed upload from the private runtime (surface attack/credential risk) or route through Redwood-hosted staging buckets (data residency/SLAs concerns).

Goal: Design and implement a flexible forwarder that supports three patterns: (1) cross-account STS-assumed role uploads to customer buckets via short-lived credentials, (2) an optional customer-managed S3-proxy gateway deployed in their VPC that accepts telemetry from the runtime and performs uploads (keeps credentials off the runtime), and (3) an offline bulk ingest path (signed transfer appliance or import/importer tool) for strict air-gapped environments. The solution must support customer-managed encryption keys lifecycle, object-level integrity verification, and resume/ retry semantics for partial multipart uploads.
acceptance_criteria:
- Forwarder supports cross-account STS role assumption with automatic credential refresh and least-privilege policy templates.
- S3-proxy deployment manifests (Helm + systemd) and operator guide produced for customer to run in VPC/on-prem.
- Offline ingest tooling with checksum manifest format and verification tests included.
- End-to-end tests demonstrating: key rotation with CMEK (customer KMS), multipart upload resume after network disruption, and a 1-hour retention recovery test.
- Console shows per-request status (queued/forwarded/failed) and downloadable verification proof (sha256) for each uploaded object.
- Security review completed and threat model updated.
- Docs: Confluence design + runbook + example IAM policies and CloudFormation/Terraform templates.
design_decisions:
1) Prefer cross-account STS as the default for cloud customers because it avoids long-lived credentials on the runtime and maps to common cloud security models. 2) Provide an S3-proxy as an opt-in pattern that customers can deploy to centralize credentials inside their network — useful for companies with strict egress policies or to integrate with on-prem object gateways. 3) Offline ingest path implemented as a verification-first tool: produce a manifest with checksums and signatures that Redwood's ingestion operator will verify before accepting. 4) Use multipart upload with a fixed anchor object containing a signed manifest to support resumability and prove provenance. 5) Encryption: support both customer-managed KMS (CMEK) and client-side encryption for air-gapped scenarios.

Trade-offs: The proxy adds an operational burden for customers (deploy+maintain) but reduces credential exposure on runtime. STS requires customers to accept cross-account role trust; some large enterprises may reject that, which is why we keep the proxy/offline paths. Multipart resume adds complexity but is necessary for unstable WAN links common in enterprise on-prem networks.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (Weeks 1-2): implement STS role-assume flow, IAM policy templates, and runtime credential rotation. Create unit tests and a minimal conformance test using a public test bucket.
Phase 2 (Weeks 3-4): build proxy reference implementation (Go) with TLS-by-default, mTLS option, and a small operator manifest for Kubernetes + systemd packaging for on-prem VMs. Provide quickstart and health endpoints.
Phase 3 (Weeks 5-6): offline ingest tooling (CLI), checksum manifest spec, and operator-side verifier. Integrate with console to display ingestion proofs.
Phase 4 (Weeks 7-8): security review, performance tests, and documentation. Prepare guided onboarding checklist for customers migrating existing audit sinks.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for STS token refresh logic and least-privilege enforcement.
- Integration tests validating multipart resume semantics using network throttling.
- E2E integration with a mock KMS to validate CMEK rotation scenarios.
- Fuzz tests for the proxy's upload path to catch header/truncation edge cases.
- Pen test scope: proxy endpoint, runtime upload code, and offline ingestion signature verification.
rollout_plan:
- Beta: selected enterprise customers willing to pilot (invite-only). Feature flag gated.
- Monitor via canary customers for 2 weeks with detailed telemetry.
- Graduate to GA after 4 successful pilots and completed security review.
- Migration guide for customers currently using Redwood-hosted staging buckets with timeline and opt-out policy.
dev_notes:
- initial prototype of STS flow in branch feat/audit-sts. See unit tests under tests/forwarder.
- We will reuse existing upload queue code but add a pluggable sink interface (sink drivers: sts, proxy, offline).
- Ensure KV cache and upload queue don't hold plaintext payload longer than necessary; encrypt at rest in local staging using ephemeral keys.
security_and_compliance:
- Threat model updated: added attacker scenarios for compromised proxy and compromised STS keys.
- Policy templates for least privilege included; recommend customers scope permission to PutObject, ListMultipartUploadParts, AbortMultipartUpload on a prefix.
- Retention mapping: support copying object lifecycle tags that customers use to enforce retention.
- Audit proofs: create a signed manifest (signed by runtime key) stored adjacent to objects to ensure non-repudiation.
runbook:
- Runbook steps for common failures: STS AssumeRole denied -> check trust policy and token thresholds. Proxy 502/timeout -> check backend health, TLS certs, and verify mTLS config. Offline ingest failure -> validate manifest checksums and verify operator signature.
- Emergency rollback: revert to routing to Redwood-hosted staging (opt-in) if customer consents; requires SLA amendment.
